When every class component lists its members in the same order, you know where to look. Lifecycle methods are at the top and `render` is at the bottom.

The default order is static methods, then lifecycle methods, then everything else, then `render`. The lifecycle methods are ordered too, roughly in the order React calls them: `constructor`, then `componentDidMount`, then `componentDidUpdate`, then `componentWillUnmount`.

The rule checks classes and `createReactClass()` objects. It ignores function components.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/sort-comp" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/sort-comp" = ["error", {
  order = ["static-methods", "lifecycle", "everything-else", "render"],
  groups = {},
}]
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
class Profile extends React.Component {
  render() {
    return <button onClick={this.handleClick}>{this.props.name}</button>;
  }

  handleClick() {
    this.props.onSelect();
  }

  componentDidMount() {
    this.props.load();
  }
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
class Profile extends React.Component {
  componentDidMount() {
    this.props.load();
  }

  handleClick() {
    this.props.onSelect();
  }

  render() {
    return <button onClick={this.handleClick}>{this.props.name}</button>;
  }
}
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `order` | `["static-methods", "lifecycle", "everything-else", "render"]` | The order. Each entry is a member name, a pattern such as `"/^handle.+$/"`, or the name of a group. |
| `groups` | `{}` | Your own groups. Each key is a group name, and each value is a list of member names and patterns. Defining `lifecycle` replaces the built-in list. |

These groups are built in:

| Group | What is in it |
| --- | --- |
| `lifecycle` | `displayName`, `propTypes`, `contextTypes`, `childContextTypes`, `mixins`, `statics`, `defaultProps`, `constructor`, `getDefaultProps`, `state`, `getInitialState`, `getChildContext`, `getDerivedStateFromProps`, `componentWillMount`, `componentDidMount`, `componentWillReceiveProps`, `shouldComponentUpdate`, `componentWillUpdate`, `getSnapshotBeforeUpdate`, `componentDidUpdate`, `componentDidCatch`, `componentWillUnmount`, in this order. Each `UNSAFE_` name comes right after the name without the prefix. |
| `static-variables`, `static-methods` | Static fields, and static methods. |
| `instance-variables`, `instance-methods` | Class fields that don't hold a function, and class fields that do. |
| `getters`, `setters` | `get` and `set` accessors. |
| `type-annotations` | Fields that have a type and no value. |
| `everything-else` | Anything no other entry matches. |

This config puts the event handlers right before the methods that render:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/sort-comp" = ["error", {
  order = ["lifecycle", "everything-else", "handlers", "rendering"],
  groups = {
    handlers = ["/^handle.+$/"],
    rendering = ["/^render.+$/", "render"],
  },
}]
```

With it, this is reported, because `handleClick` comes before `fullName`:

{/* bad {"options": [{"order": ["lifecycle", "everything-else", "handlers", "rendering"], "groups": {"handlers": ["/^handle.+$/"], "rendering": ["/^render.+$/", "render"]}}]} */}
```jsx
class Profile extends React.Component {
  handleClick() {
    this.props.onSelect();
  }

  fullName() {
    return this.props.first + " " + this.props.last;
  }

  render() {
    return <button onClick={this.handleClick}>{this.fullName()}</button>;
  }
}
```

And this isn't:

{/* good {"options": [{"order": ["lifecycle", "everything-else", "handlers", "rendering"], "groups": {"handlers": ["/^handle.+$/"], "rendering": ["/^render.+$/", "render"]}}]} */}
```jsx
class Profile extends React.Component {
  fullName() {
    return this.props.first + " " + this.props.last;
  }

  handleClick() {
    this.props.onSelect();
  }

  renderName() {
    return <span>{this.fullName()}</span>;
  }

  render() {
    return <button onClick={this.handleClick}>{this.renderName()}</button>;
  }
}
```
